I would keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the cropping pattern I trust most because it fits the local climate, matches the irrigation conditions, and gives me the most stable income over a full year. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I would focus first on water and fertilizer during jointing and grain filling, and I would watch closely for aphids, rust, and dry hot wind. After wheat harvest, I would quickly sow summer maize on the same land to avoid losing moisture and heat. For seed, I would use improved or hybrid varieties because I care more about steady yield and lodging resistance than saving seed money. I would not make the plan too complicated with many small crops, because with my situation I would rather manage two familiar crops well than spread my labor and cash too thin. I would use moderate fertilizer, several key irrigations, routine pest control, and mainly rotary tillage because it is practical and affordable for me.
